answer_1.quote: Existing methods for stylistic text rewriting ... adapting the text to a particular style while preserving its originally intended meaning ... we present a comprehensive analysis of the need for context in stylistic rewriting ...
answer_1.outputs: Stylistically rewritten sentences (e.g., formal/informal, toxic/less‑toxic, sentiment‑changed) conditioned on preceding context

answer_2.quote: We use word‑overlap metrics like ROUGE, METEOR and word error rate (WER) for lexical similarity... To measure semantic similarity we use BERTScore and SBERT, as well as Smatch... For fluency we employ GPT‑2 perplexity... we introduce CtxSimFit, a new composite metric that combines contextual cohesiveness and semantic similarity.

answer_4.quote: We conduct a head‑to‑head human evaluation of non‑contextual and contextual rewrites ... Participants are given preceding context, pairs of rewritten sentences ... and are then asked to rank the rewrites with respect to: Naturalness, Style Strength, Event‑level Similarity, Intended Meaning, Overall Fit.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators compare each pair of rewrites (contextual vs. non‑contextual) given the same preceding context and rank them on the listed dimensions.
